_: Differences that are deliberate. nightbar.css is Vale's first design; the review that followed amended parts of it, and the toolkit refused others. Anything listed here is subtracted from the score so the ranking only shows real drift.
gauges: arcs start at 12 o'clock, not the design's 6 (from 180deg) -- Vale's review asked for it so the three read as one cluster
one hue #4d9dff on a #16294a track, amber and red reserved for thresholds
value and unit are drawn into the SVG; a GtkLabel carries one type size
the middle gauge is MEM, not the design's DISK: there is no disk sampler and memory is the vital that was already being watched
no history trace: there is no sampler, and a faked one is worse than none
toggles: tile gradient stays in CSS rather than in the rail SVG: a file with a linearGradient in it loads through gdk-pixbuf and then draws nothing
actions: faders are not vertical and do not sit beside the grid: swaync hardcodes Gtk.Orientation.HORIZONTAL and packs widgets in one vertical box
sliders: horizontal, below the actions, same reason
notifications: swaync groups by app and stacks a group's rows; there is no option to turn that off
head: the design's mono clock letter-spaces its digits in the reference render, because Ubuntu's Nerd Font Mono patch pads every glyph to one cell. The build uses Inter with tabular figures instead
